**Stillingsbeskrivelse

**_We are looking for a driven Business Controller with a strong motivation for FP&A to join Netcompany DK. You are either a recent graduate or have 1–3 years of experience, and you will play a central role in ensuring timely and accurate management reporting, as well as in-depth analyses of our business and financial KPIs. You will become part of a dynamic team where collaboration across departments and with different stakeholders is a natural part of everyday life.

_**Your Responsibilities

**You will become part of a well-functioning and collaborative team where you will have plenty of opportunities to share ideas, learn from colleagues, and grow professionally. Working closely with the Head of Finance NBS and DK, you will take ownership of key aspects of the monthly financial reporting to management. This includes following up on our business areas and preparing presentations.

In addition to being responsible for your own areas, you will have a broad range of stakeholders, where collaboration with the other Shared Services departments in the business is an important part of the role. The position will give you unique insight into the financial value drivers of the company and an understanding of the financial parameters that drive a business.

**Your Responsibilites Will Typically Include

**

• Conducting business analyses

• Comment on monthly reports for your areas of responsibility

• Contributing to the continuous improvement of the monthly reporting process

• Participating with your own areas of responsibility in the development of our system structure

• Actively participating in the budgeting and forecasting processes

**About You

**As a person, you are motivated by working with both complex and operational tasks, and you possess the ability to communicate across the organization. You have a proactive mindset and strong business acumen, combined with excellent analytical skills. You take initiative, identify opportunities for improvement, and are motivated by contributing to the development of the organization. With a keen eye for detail and a strong focus on quality, you take pride in delivering accurate results and meeting deadlines in a structured and reliable manner.

**To Succeed In This Role, You

**

• Are newly graduated or at the beginning of your career within a Cand.Merc. (Master of Science in Business and Economics), for example Cand.Merc.Fir, Cand.Merc.Asc, Cand.Merc.Aef., or similar education.

• Have experience working in Excel and processing large volumes of data.

• Are initiative-taking and are keen to contribute to improving and developing processes. At the same time, you have an eye for detail and work in a structured manner.

• Full professional proficiency in Danish and English (written and spoken) is a must.

**Join an inclusive community

**At Netcompany, we highly prioritise an inclusive community. We actively promote an open and welcoming work culture based on collaboration and mutual trust, where there is always an opportunity for sparring.

As part of our culture and values, all employees, regardless of background, identity, and experience, are met with understanding and respect and given equal opportunities for development and well-being.

As we are an international company with offices in many countries, you will have the opportunity to learn and collaborate internationally with colleagues from across the world. We offer a shared environment where we engage with each other across departments and projects. Additionally, we have a wide range of social and professional events that provide you with the best opportunities to expand and build a network early in your career.

**Send us your application

**Upload your resume and a motivational letter to our recruitment system via the link. If you have unanswered questions, feel free to write to hr.dk@netcompany.com.

_All qualified candidates are encouraged to apply regardless of gender, gender expression, sexuality, disability, age, religion and belief, political views, nationality, ethnicity, or social background.

_We are committed to creating an inclusive and diverse environment. Our recruitment processes are based on individual merit. If you require any reasonable adjustments or additional support during the interview process, please email our recruiters at reasonableadjustments@netcompany.com for assistance.

At Trustpilot, we're on an incredible journey. We're a profitable, high-growth FTSE-250 company with a big vision: to become the universal symbol of trust. We run the world's largest open customer review platform, and while we've come a long way, there's still so much exciting work to do. Come join us at the heart of trust!

Our growing sales organisation is compensated through commission, and our Global Sales Planning & Compensation team structures those plans, sets sales targets, and ensures every salesperson worldwide is paid accurately and on time. Acting as the company’s behavioural economists, we partner with commercial leadership to analyse how incentives drive revenue growth, which gives us an inside view across the entire sales journey, from revenue planning to performance and pay.

We are looking for a Student Assistant to join our Global Sales Planning & Compensation team in Copenhagen, reporting to the Sales Compensation Manager. This is a hands-on, part-time role with hours planned flexibly around your studies and exam periods. From day one, you will take ownership of real processes that directly impact how colleagues are paid and how leadership tracks performance, working across Sales, Finance, and HR in Denmark, the UK, and the US.

To thrive in this role, you bring strong analytical instincts, a sharp eye for detail, and genuine curiosity about how incentives shape commercial behaviour. Experience with Salesforce, Forma, or similar business tools is a plus, but not required.

What you’ll be doing:

• Support the monthly and quarterly commission cycle to ensure accurate, on-time global payouts.

• Investigate and resolve commission questions from sales colleagues, explaining data outcomes clearly.

• Upload and reconcile sales targets across our systems and help prepare and launch commission plans.

• Run recurring reports and build leadership presentation packs that turn numbers into actionable insights.

• Coordinate administration for our sales recognition programmes.

• Help develop our commission system (Forma), build controls, and document repeatable standard operating procedures while working across Forma, Salesforce, and Sage.

• Collaborate with colleagues in the UK and US across Commercial, Revenue Operations, FP&A, Payroll, Accounting, and HR.

Who you are:

• In the final year of a Bachelor's degree, or early in a Master's, in finance, economics, or a related field.

• Skilled in Excel or Google Sheets (lookups, pivot tables, and clean, structured models) with a strong interest in numbers and data.

• Analytical, detail-oriented and proactive, you catch anomalies in data and spot ways to improve processes.

• Commercially curious and eager to learn how sales compensation and incentives drive revenue in a global tech company.

• A clear, concise communicator who handles confidential pay and performance data with care.

• Collaborative, fluent in English, and able to work regularly from our Copenhagen office.

What’s in it for you:

• 
Learn how sales compensation works in a global technology company, from plan design to payout, and how commercial leaders use incentives to influence behaviour and reach revenue goals.

• 
Hands-on experience in a function that connects Sales, Finance and HR.

• 
Ownership of real processes that directly affect how our sales colleagues are paid.

• 
Flexible hours that fit around your studies and exam periods.

• 
A strong foundation for a career in finance, commercial operations or reward.

• 
Rich learning and development opportunities are supported through the Trustpilot Academy and Blinkist

• 
Central office with  a laid-back vibe and constant buzz of different languages being spoken everywhere you go It’s complete with a coffee bar, canteen, and table tennis and has a wide variety of refreshments available - you can opt-in for breakfast and lunch at an affordable price

• 
Regular opportunities to connect and get to know your fellow Trusties, including company-wide celebrations and events, Trustie Community activities, and team socials

• 
Opportunity to join the Trustpilot Social Club for a small monthly fee and attend regular social and leisure activities like go-karting, cooking classes, and escape rooms

Transformational Change Manager | Financial Services | Copenhagen, Denmark

Are you ready to lead teams and drive impactful change at scale for financial services clients? Are you passionate about helping organizations successfully navigate transformation, and do you bring both strategic vision and hands-on delivery experience? Then the role of Transformational Change Manager in Copenhagen is your next career move. Let’s build the future of work—together.

About the Team and the Role

As a Manager within our Talent team, based in Copenhagen, Denmark, you will take ownership of end-to-end project delivery, client relationships, and account management, with financial services as your primary industry focus. You will guide teams in co-creating and implementing human-centered transformation strategies, develop change approaches that are agile and ready for the digital world, and ensure the realization of measurable business outcomes.

You will work primarily with leading financial services clients, including banks, insurance providers, and capital markets firms, partnering with them on digital, technology-driven, and organizational transformations. You will be part of multidisciplinary teams delivering large, complex programs, working closely with client teams and international colleagues to solve challenging organizational problems, lead key workstreams, guide junior colleagues, and deliver specific project outcomes. Explore our point of view and Talent offering here.

The Work

• Lead Transformation Journeys – Help financial services clients navigate complex transformations, building organizations that are more capable, resilient, and adaptable to redirection and ambiguity.

• Human-Centered Change Strategies – Translate strategic direction and business objectives into holistic, agile change strategies that address culture, ways of working, and readiness for the future.

• Deep Change Management Expertise – Drive leadership alignment to the change vision, activate change using insight-driven approaches leveraging AI, engage large-scale change networks, and prepare organizations for business readiness, technology adoption, and new ways of working.

• Workforce Reinvention – Shape organization design, reskilling, and upskilling strategies for new operating models (e.g., S/4HANA, GBS, human-agentic workforce) and prepare the workforce for emerging roles.

• Technology Enablement – Unlock the human potential of new technologies through enterprise-wide system implementations, digital learning platforms, and AI-enabled change activation.

• Data-Driven Insights – Use analytics and predictive tools to measure adoption, sentiment, and transformation impact.

• Stakeholder Engagement & Account Management – Build trusted relationships with C-level executives and client teams in financial services, oversee account health, and proactively identify opportunities to expand our footprint.

• Business Development – Build trusted client relationships, identifying new growth opportunities, supporting business development activities, and shaping go-to-market strategies.

You will also:

• Lead workstreams and coach junior colleagues, bringing together cross-functional teams and specialists.

• Collaborate with Financial Services clients, the Netherlands & Nordics Talent practice and Accenture’s international network of experts.

• Balance changing priorities and timelines while keeping delivery focused on practical, measurable outcomes.

• Contribute to an inclusive, supportive team culture and continue developing your expertise in Change & Transformation Management.

About You

You bring a background in management consulting, organizational change or business transformation, with experience delivering people-centered change in complex, technology-enabled programs. You understand the opportunities and challenges facing banks, insurers and capital markets firms as they modernize systems, redesign operating models and introduce new ways of working. Your project experience may include roles such as Change Manager, Transformation Lead, Organizational Change Lead, Change and Communications Lead or Business Project Manager.

You are passionate about the people side of transformation and about turning strategic ambitions into meaningful, measurable change. You can align leaders around a shared vision, engage stakeholders and change networks, and shape communication, training and adoption activities that help people embrace new technologies, processes and behaviors. You use data and feedback to assess readiness, measure adoption and improve your approach iteratively.

You are comfortable leading workstreams and multidisciplinary teams in fast-paced, complex environments, combining strategic thinking with hands-on delivery. You build trusted relationships with senior client stakeholders, coach junior colleagues and solve problems in a people-oriented, insight-driven way. Most importantly, you are a collaborative colleague who helps teams navigate uncertainty and achieve outcomes together.

Requirements

• 
5+ years of relevant experience in organizational change, future workforce and/ or Human Resources; for example, guiding organizations in their transformation journey, designing and implementing large-scale communication and training programs, or upskill leaders to carry out desired behaviors.

• 
Management consulting experience or experience working within Financial Services, is a plus, not a prerequisite

• 
Strong consulting skills and the ability to engage senior business and HR stakeholders

• 
Strong self-leadership, with experience leading workstreams, collaborating in teams and coaching junior colleagues

• 
Understanding of organizational change and transformation components and complexicty, preferably within financial services and knowledge of banking, insurance, or capital markets transformation challenges

• 
A commercial mindset, the ability to build trusted client networks and a focus on measurable business and workforce outcomes

• 
Experience collaborating with cross-functional project teams in a global environment

• 
Professional proficiency in English; Danish language skills is an advantage for local client engagement, but not a requirement

• 
Track record as people-oriented, insight driven and iterative problem solver

• 
A master’s degree in a relevant field, such as business, engineering, or behavioral and social sciences

What We Offer

• Membership in our growing Netherlands & Nordics Talent team, with access to a global network of experts at the forefront of talent reinvention

• The opportunity to shape your career around your aspirations, with regular support from your People Lead

• A competitive salary, bonus schemes, health insurance, an employee share purchase program, and other benefits

• A strong commitment to employee well-being and work-life balance, including flexible arrangements that support family life, mental health, and well-being

• A supportive, encouraging and fun team who always roots for one another

• Market-leading expertise, a steep learning curve and great opportunities for development

• Opportunities to participate in corporate citizenship initiatives, including volunteering, charity work, and Inclusion & Diversity networks

Alfa Laval Nordic are currently looking for a Marine International Service Engineer to join our team in Denmark.

Every day, we get opportunities to make a positive impact – on our colleagues, partners, customers, and society. Together, we’re pioneering the solutions of the future and unlocking the full potential of precious resources. Trusted to act on initiative, we challenge conventional thinking to develop world leading technologies that inspire progress in vital areas, including energy, food, water and shipping. As we push forward, the innovative, open spirit that fuels our 140-year-old start-up culture and rapid growth also drives our personal growth. So, as we shape a more resourceful, less wasteful world, we build careers too.

About the job

As a Marine Field Service Engineer you will help keep critical maritime operations running safely, efficiently, and reliably. In this customer-facing role, you will support the installation, commissioning, troubleshooting, maintenance, and optimization of marine equipment onboard vessels and at customer sites worldwide.

Working closely with shipowners, crews, and service teams, you will solve technical challenges in real operating environments while contributing to improved equipment performance, reduced downtime, and long-term operational efficiency. You will play an important role in delivering responsive service, building trusted customer relationships, and supporting the maritime industry’s ongoing transition toward more energy-efficient operations.

This is an opportunity for a hands-on engineer who enjoys problem-solving, international collaboration and travelling (minimum 150 days a year), and working at the forefront of marine service and technology.

This role will be based in Denmark, with the ideal located in either Kolding, Soborg or Copenhagen.

Your duties will include:

• 
Execute international and local field service jobs within Alfa Laval portfolio that are requested through the International Marine Service Desk;

• 
Perform troubleshooting, to solve the customer’s problem, with full autonomy within the job scope on board of vessels in the requested port; if needed, sail with a vessel until the problem is solved;

• 
Change components, upgrade equipment and control systems, perform re-commissioning, perform safety checks and adjustments, and advise and coach customers and crew in product usage;

• 
Execute Inspections, Condition Audits and Sensor Exchange;

• 
Consult if needed Global Technical Specialists before, during and after the field service;

• 
Build relations with customers and crew;

• 
Report and document performed field service as per guidelines;

• 
Pick-up and bring bookings, VISAs, permits, spare parts, equipment etc. needed to perform the field service;

• 
Work together with other International Marine Service Organization members as a team, and act as a technical support backup to Global Technical Specialists and Global Coordinators if so required; use and support the ISE network pro-actively, share findings with colleagues;

• 
Travel to execute marine service jobs, participate in trainings, team meetings etc., primarily in Europe, but also globally when needed.

Do you want to be a valued part of the critical infrastructure that serves communities across Europe and beyond? Are you looking for an opportunity where you can make an impact, shape decisions, and accelerate your career?

If so, we are looking for dedicated, curious, and highly motivated graduates to join the DFDS Graduate Programme starting in September 2027.

**Be part of the movement - and play your part

**About The Role The DFDS Graduate Programme is a two-year fast-track programme for recent graduates with an interest in and passion for the maritime industry.

During the programme, you will complete three rotations across different areas of our Ferry Division. You will begin at our headquarters in Copenhagen, followed by a mandatory international rotation at one of our European hubs. Your final rotation at our headquarters will be tailored to your skills, interests, and our business needs.

Throughout the programme, you will gain broad exposure to both the operational and commercial sides of our Ferry Division while building valuable industry knowledge and professional experience.

Ferry Operations offers broad end-to-end exposure with sustainability, standardisation, and digitalisation at the heart of everything we do.

**Examples Of Interesting Tasks Could Be To:

**

• Help design and develop the vessels of tomorrow, supporting our green transition through electrification, ammonia, and green methanol initiatives.

• Support the operation and maintenance of our fleet of more than 70 RoRo, RoPax, and passenger vessels, covering everything from dry dock planning to crisis management and contingency handling.

• Contribute to our standardisation and digitalisation journey across eight owned terminals and more than 20 third-party terminals, where safety remains our highest priority.

• Support fleet planning, equipment optimisation, and our intercontinental rail setup, connecting ferry and logistics operations across our network.

In the commercial part of our Ferry Division, you will work alongside colleagues across Europe, supporting both B2B and B2C markets.

**Examples Of Interesting Tasks Could Be To:

**

• Support local and global sales teams and assist with key account management, ensuring our network is successfully marketed and sold across regions.

• Drive continuous improvement in customer service and booking processes through standardisation and digitalisation initiatives.

• Collaborate with IT teams to enhance and optimise our digital customer offerings.

• Work with operational teams to optimise routes and vessel capacity to meet customer demand.

• Support revenue management activities, including pricing optimisation and commercial performance analysis.

Across all rotations, you will work closely with highly skilled colleagues and engage with customers, suppliers, and partners throughout the maritime value chain. To support your development, each rotation will include both a dedicated manager and a mentor who will help you successfully navigate your learning journey.

Alongside hands-on experience at DFDS, you will participate in the Danish Shipping Education Programme, delivered by Danish Shipping. This programme consists of webinars, four seminars in Denmark, and one international seminar, covering key topics across the maritime industry.

****About You

****At DFDS, we believe the strongest teams are built on diversity, inclusion, and different perspectives. We are looking for candidates who:

• Have graduated from a relevant master’s degree by the start of the Graduate Programme in September 2027, preferably within maritime studies, supply chain, freight forwarding, logistics, sustainability, business, finance, engineering, or a related field.

• Have gained relevant experience through a student job, internship, exchange programme, or other extracurricular activities.

• Have no more than two years of full-time professional experience after completing your master's degree.

• Demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Are collaborative team players who enjoy working with others and creating impact.

• Are curious, proactive, and eager to learn and develop professionally.

• Have an international mindset and are excited about working across cultures and locations.

Working at DFDS **Join the movement and grow with us

**As part of the DFDS Graduate Programme, you will become part of a strong graduate network across the company and build valuable connections across our international business. We offer a steep learning curve, meaningful responsibility from day one, and three interesting rotations designed to accelerate your professional development.

Are we a match? Apply now.  If your skills, experience, aspirations, and personality match this opportunity, we would love to hear from you.

Please Apply By Uploading Your CV no Later Than 30 November 2026. When Applying, You’re Also Asked To Answer The Following Questions:

• Why are you interested in joining the DFDS Graduate Programme?

• How will the programme help kickstart your career?

• How do you expect to contribute to the programme and DFDS?

• What do you believe will be your biggest challenge(s) during the programme?

**We look forward to hearing from you.

We're building KickOff, our next-generation GitOps platform. You'll join during a pivotal moment: we're actively migrating services to KickOff, establishing new platform patterns and enabling 100+ engineers to ship faster and more reliably. We also maintain separate on-premises Kubernetes clusters running model training and video processing workloads.

This isn't a "keep the lights on" role. You'll shape platform architecture, drive technical decisions, and directly impact engineering velocity across both cloud and on-prem environments.

**What You Will Do

**You'll join the platform engineering team that owns these areas together. We share ownership, pair on complex work, and rotate responsibilities.

• Evolve KickOff (our GitOps platform) to improve developer experience.

• Support service migrations to KickOff, partnering with product teams.

• Maintain and optimize KickOff on AWS EKS.

• Manage our on-premises Kubernetes clusters running ML training workloads.

• Establish monitoring, alerting, and observability using LGTM.

• Debug distributed systems spanning multiple environments.

• Create documentation and tooling that makes infrastructure approachable

As the platform matures, you'll have opportunities to shape multi-cluster architecture, GPU workload scheduling, disaster recovery strategy, and cloud provider independence.

**What You Could Bring

**We're looking for someone with 3-5 years running production infrastructure, including:

• Production Kubernetes: You've operated K8s in production and understand the operational reality, not just tutorials.

• Platform-as-product mindset: You've built internal tooling that real teams use, gathered feedback, and measured impact on productivity.

• Infrastructure as Code: Strong Terraform, Crossplane, or similar experience.

• Observability: You've implemented monitoring and alerting that helps teams operate confidently.

• Security awareness: You know how to embed security into platform design without slowing teams down.

• Problem-solving: You debug complex distributed systems and design practical solutions.

• Collaboration: You work through discussion and feedback, share context effectively.

Nice to have: GitOps tools (Flux, ArgoCD), Cilium, multi-cloud architecture, on-prem K8s experience.

**How We Work

**You’ll join a Copenhagen-based platform team of 5 engineers with shared ownership of KickOff and our on-prem Kubernetes clusters. We work closely together day to day through pairing, code reviews, and a rotating ownership model for operational responsibilities and platform improvements.

You’ll collaborate regularly with the Processing Platform team on workload needs, reliability, and developer experience, and you’ll use feedback from product and engineering teams to shape platform priorities and improve how teams build and ship on KickOff.

We work pragmatically and iterate quickly. We document decisions, favor simple solutions where possible, and focus on tooling and platform patterns that help teams move faster with confidence.

Our Copenhagen office mirrors our innovative technology – with an indoor ball court, rooftop terrace, and well-equipped gym. We have created a facility that supports connecting disciplines across the business, facilitates creative thinking, and gives the space to engage with colleagues, our global partners, and the entire Veo community.

Values we hold at Veo:

Dare - We take initiative, stay curious, and challenge the status quo in our work.

Own it - We drive impact by identifying opportunities, taking responsibility, and confidently executing.

Level up - We embrace growth, continuously learning and shaping our skills.

Play as a team - We collaborate across a diverse organization, leveraging shared insights for stronger

Customer Centric - We deliver value by having close partnerships and a deep understanding of our customers (internally and externally)

**The position

**The Head of Regulatory Affairs & Compliance is responsible for leading the day-to-day central Regulatory Affairs & Compliance function, with primary responsibility for Omnigame’s B2C operator regulatory framework and for coordinating consistent regulatory standards, methodologies and governance across the wider business.

The role reports to the Chief Legal & Compliance Officer, who retains executive-level legal and regulatory strategy, overall oversight and escalation of material regulatory risk, Board-level reporting, significant legal interpretation, contractual/legal matters and major regulatory or enforcement matters.

**Key Responsibilities

**

• Own and coordinate the central operational regulatory affairs and compliance framework, while supporting consistent regulatory standards and governance across Omnigame’s B2C and B2B activities.

• Lead and coordinate Omnigame’s central regulatory licensing portfolio and support the Chief Legal & Compliance Officer and relevant business owners with applications, renewals, variations, notifications and ongoing licence obligations.

• Act as a principal operational point of contact, together with the Chief Legal & Compliance Officer, for gambling regulators and coordinate regulatory correspondence, inspections, enquiries and submissions, escalating material matters to the Chief Legal & Compliance Officer.

• Assist with regulatory assessments for entry into new jurisdictions and ensure that market-entry requirements are identified, allocated and implemented.

• Own the regulatory reporting framework, including reporting calendars, quality assurance, submission governance and evidence of compliance.

• Lead regulatory change management: monitor developments, assess applicability and impact, allocate implementation actions, track remediation and ensure appropriate evidence and governance.

• Set or coordinate group-level compliance standards relevant to B2B counterparty due diligence where required and provide support or challenge on material matters.

• Coordinate cross-company regulatory standards for game, product and platform compliance and support material or cross-functional regulatory matters.

• Develop, maintain and improve compliance policies, procedures, controls, registers and monitoring arrangements.

• Identify material regulatory risks and control gaps, establish remediation plans and provide appropriate escalation and reporting to the Chief Legal & Compliance Officer.

• Coordinate and oversee regulatory audits, assurance activities, inspections and responses to regulator information requests with assistance from relevant Regulatory Affairs Specialist.

• Partner with Product, Technology, Commercial, Operations, AML and Safer Gambling to embed regulatory requirements into business processes and change initiatives.

• Lead, allocate and quality-assure the work of direct Regulatory Affairs & Compliance team members and support their professional development.

• Promote clear ownership, consistent working methods and effective knowledge-sharing between the central Regulatory Affairs & Compliance function and embedded compliance resources.

• Prepare management information and regulatory/compliance reporting for the Chief Legal & Compliance Officer and other relevant governance forums.

• Support the Chief Legal & Compliance Officer in implementing the wider legal and compliance strategy and in material regulatory projects.

**Qualifications And Experience

**
